transcript.text: Hello folks, we do have some exciting news for RuneScape Dragon Isles today as coming very soon we have our first
Luminates update. This should arrive within the next week or so and marks the first of three substantial content
updates to the game between now and December. Alongside everything within the Luminates update, we also have a few
comments from a private Q&A at RuneFest where the devs remark on bringing a new line of inventory space to the game
taking the max limit from 24 to 32 as well as introducing new ways to summon not to be confused with the summoning
skill itself though, but summoning mechanics that already exist like spells and the Pharaoh's Scepter. Anyway,
plenty for us to get through and as always we are not wasting any time, so let's get started.
Okay, so first things first the Luminates update itself will drop in stages, so we'll have a sizable update
sometime this month likely in a week or so's time and then another mid-November followed by a third and much more
significant update sometime in December. That will then conclude the Luminates update as a whole, but it also means
that all of the following content will arrive at various points between now and then. To begin we first have the
introduction of elves being added to the game. Elves appear to be part of the core theme for the 2027 roadmap and so
with Luminates acting as a prelude to the Blood Crystal Saga, it does make sense as to why we're being introduced
to them now. The two main characters for the story for now would be Ceridwen and
Morwen. Ceridwen is an elven bard who we must help protect her baby and uncover secrets towards a larger mystery, whilst
Morwen is a mysterious bounty hunter on the task of tracking Ceridwen down and will likely act as the main boss to this
section of the story. Through Ceridwen's talents as a bard, we will acquire a lyre through this questline which will
be very important to not only harmonizing with song stones for the story, but also traveling through fairy
rings and gathering harmonized crystal fragments. Song stones appear to be integral to the main questline here,
however, we don't know the full ins and outs right now. It appears we will have to locate these on our adventures and
they may be quite tricky to find at times. We would then use the lyre to harmonize with the stone itself, likely
acting as a puzzle / mini-game. And then, upon successfully harmonizing, we would gain crystal fragments as well as
unlock a harmony for the lyre, which should be important for the main questline, but may have other gameplay
purposes outside of this. As for the fairy rings, we will need the lyre to first harmonize and then travel through
them. Just like the song stones, we've no idea how any of this specifically works right now, but it is said that
they will take us to many new areas and secret places. It's possible that outside of this, they may become another
convenient method of fast travel. And it's also likely that they themselves involve some kind of puzzle-solving or
mini-game, at least for the first time that we ever use them. Finally, the harmonized crystal fragments that we
acquire from harmonizing with song stones and maybe able to acquire through other means are basically a resource or
currency that we can use to acquire new weapons, armor, and vestiges. Weapons and armor are pretty self-explanatory,
and whilst we have a little bit of concept art for them right here, we don't truly know how it all looks or
what's exactly available. We can expect at least one or two new sets for melee, ranged, and magic playstyles though, as
well as a vast range of different weapon types. Then, as for vestiges, these are
basically the items you identify in game to acquire the blueprint or recipe to a new piece of equipment. The game is
actually stuffed with tons of these already, ranging from weapons, armor, capes, jewelry, and whatever else. And
so, we can basically expect a handful of new additions to be added in. Now, outside of the crystal fragments being
used to craft or buy various things, it's likely other equipment and whatnot will also be available outside of
needing to use these fragments, such as weapons and armor being quest rewards or various different vestiges being
treasure in a dungeon, etc. Quite excitingly though, outside of the weapons, armor, and vestiges mentioned
already, we do also have new elf-themed equipment being added in. Now, I'm not entirely sure what exactly falls under
the equipment title, as I'd assume it means everything from weapons, armor, and accessories all the way up to tools
and whatever else. But, it was specifically stated we are getting new elf-themed equipment separate to the
concept art that was shown. And so, quite a bit of variety. The next big addition we have is the Alven-themed
building kit. This is, of course, floors, walls, ceilings, roofs, pillars, fences, and then a few of the bits and
pieces, and will mirror out most of the same Alven architecture in game. Interestingly enough, it's mentioned
that the upcoming update Song of Rebellion, which arrives over January, February, and then March of 2027, also
brings along a large Alven city, suggesting that whilst elves and Alven-themed questline and an entirely
new area will be added in with this Luminance update, we will have to wait until next year before we get the full
Alven experience. For now, though, we do absolutely have the building kit arriving within the next couple of
months. Alongside the building kit, we also have additional Alven features being added to the character
customization, too. We have features for both male and female models, as well as Alven ears to complement them. And you
can change your character's appearance in game whenever you like. Previously, there was an issue with the character
customization creating issues for players, and so the devs have temporarily disabled it. But, outside of
this issue, players can customize appearance for free whenever they like. Now, the final big addition for the
Luminance update, and possibly the most anticipated, would be the introduction of the prayer skill. Prayer will work a
little differently in Dragon Wilds to other RuneScape games in that there is no prayer flicking, but we do still
acquire blessings and powers from the skill itself. We need to craft an altar and base and possibly various other
stations as we progress the skill. These will allow us to do things like burn incense, scatter ashes, and bury bones,
which will, of course, then allow us to tap into the previously mentioned blessings and powers. There should be
more to it than this, but that is what's been teased so far. We will also have a 1 through to 99 progression track for
prayer, as well as various spells we should unlock, too. And so, as much as we do know already, there's still plenty
to surprise us. The last few things to cover for the Luminance update itself would just be that there are more NPCs
arriving than just Caridwin and Morwen. These other NPCs will then likely offer various quests and mini-games, as well
as hopefully act as one or two traders. And then, we know very little about the new lands actually being added in. Other
than that, there will be lots of trees, as is expected with owls, but then the concept art points towards lush and
beautiful which I'm sure we'll see fully explored throughout 2027's road map. Now, unless explicitly stated otherwise,
everything I've just mentioned is arriving within the next couple of months. However, we've no idea in what
order or exactly when. It's likely that the bulk of all of this will arrive in December, as that will be the biggest of
the three upcoming updates. But then, we do still absolutely stand to receive some of this both in roughly a week's
time and sometime mid-November, too. What is also important to consider is this isn't everything that will arrive.
The devs have only showcased so much, so aside from all that I've gone through already, we will get various bits and
pieces of other new content, like new materials to acquire, enemies to fight, dungeons to explore, fish to catch,
plants to grow, etc. As well as then big chunks of quality of life, like reworks to combat, skills, and whatever else.
Some of it is mentioned and showcased, whereas other bits haven't been, and so we'll just have to wait for each and
every update itself to see just what exactly is being added or improved. Now, separate to the Dragon Wild Summit and
everything coming in the 2027 road map that I haven't mentioned for today, there was an official Q&A that took
place for the game at RuneFest. However, it wasn't filmed or live-streamed, so we have no public access to it. We may or
may not get a transcript from the devs at a future date, but for now, we do have one or two convenient posts made by
a fan in attendance, and so I wanted to touch on some of the new things coming to the game that the devs have
mentioned. Firstly, they spoke about how they plan to add a new line of inventory
to the game. This would take us from 24 to 32 slots. However, we've no idea if they spoke about weight limit or when
this addition may actually arrive in the game. It could be with the Luminates updates or it may be sometime next year.
As a quick FYI though, this is pretty big as by increasing your agility level in game, you can already increase your
max weight limit making the additional inventory space quite viable despite weight limitations. Then we have the
devs mentioning that more summoning will be arriving in the future. As things currently stand, the Pharaoh scepter in
game will allow for you to summon a cow fight worker which will attack enemies for you. And then we do have a range of
summon spells, too. And so with what they're saying here, we can likely expect more spells to arrive that allow
us to summon things as well as items that work in a similar way to the scepter. Now, it is possible there's
some more juicy stuff in this Q&A, but we just don't have access to it right now. If and when it does arrive, I'll
comb through and make a video if one but otherwise, that is all we have on it right now. Other than everything
mentioned thus far, we do of course have a decent outline to the 2027 roadmap right now. I covered it already in this
video here which is timestamped, so do feel free to check that out if you would like to. Otherwise, I'm sure once 2027
arrives and the roadmap begins, we will get more information regarding everything. As they have said, we're
getting four new skills next year. They've confirmed Hunter for early next year and Slayer for the end, but we've
no idea what the two planned for midyear could be. And then of course, as much as
they've shared, there's still a ton that will be a surprise. And so as always, we will just have to wait and see. As and
when we do get more announcements and updates though, I will be reporting on them all immediately as I've already
done with Dragon Wilds for a number of weeks now. This channel mainly focuses on Souls-likes and action RPGs, but has
